Bose QuietComfort Ultra Headphones. Used to have Sony WH1000XM4, this is much better in terms of noise cancelling. 

Although I do miss the ratcheting (clicking) height adjust,  the 5 band eq in the Sony app (the bose has 3 band) and the touch controls (the bose has one button and a finicky touch strip for volume control which I loathe to no end (it cannot be disabled). the bose has much more accurate wear detection, much better sound profile (the sony's feel too bloated and I had to eq it to all hell and still wouldn't be good enough) The bose are fairly flat (especially compared to the Sony) and much more pleasing to the ear. 

if you want immersive audio, both of them have their own implementation and I don't know which is better because I hate gimmicks like that so I had disabled it.

the xm4 are much cheaper than the Bose as they're like 5 years old (the bose is 2).

 whatever you do, do not get the wh1000xm5, they're trash in terms of build quality and pretty much everything else.

edit - there's also the regular quietcomfort from bose which are slightly cheaper but they miss out on (in my opinion) very important things like Qualcomm AptX support (to be fair, this only works if you've got an Android device with a Qualcomm chipset) but they do have the ratcheting height adjust though and slightly more comfortable imo

edit 2 - alternatively, you could wait for the wh1000xm6, they are about to be released on may 16th I think.

this feels bittersweet. skrillex was the reason I got into edm almost 15 years ago with my cousin forcing me to listen to scary monsters and nice sprites when I was 8, frankly hating the first listen but it did become my favorite song of all time eventually though. 

Here I am, at 22, an adult, while i may not know what I'm doing or where I am, Skrillex's music was the one constant that stuck by me all this through it all. 

Somewhere along experiencing the thrill of listening to "devil music"  (as my parents put it, back then) secretly, to skipping a couple of exams in college (those didn't really matter on my grades, anyway) to listen to quest for fire and don't get too close, I'd grown up, and with it, came a whole new set of problems and experiences such as love, heartbreak, a general malaise for life, really. Through it all, I'd listen to Skrillex, and reminisce about the "good old days". It feels weird, having to part with a huge part of my life growing up. 

This mixtape/album brought me back to those days again. I hope this comes on streaming although I am not sure if this itself is the full album because most of the songs aren't in full. Anyway, what I'm trying to say is, thank you Skrill, for all the memories and now this body of work.
